issues.description: ACL root field complects authorization decision with namespace ancestry — three concerns in one boolean-turned-pointer
issues.detail: The `root *namespace.Namespace` field now encodes three facts: (1) is this a root policy, (2) which namespace owns it, (3) implicit ancestry check against the request. nil-pointer-as-bool plus HasParent at check time is COMPLECTED. A small value type like `rootScope{ns *Namespace}` or explicit `IsRoot bool; RootScope *Namespace` separates 'has root policy' from 'scope of root'. The current shape will be misread.

issues.description: NamespaceSealed is a stub that always returns false — a lie shaped like a fact
issues.detail: `(*Core).NamespaceSealed` unconditionally returns false with a TODO. Callers (ListAllNamespaces filtering, future ACL gates) will be written against this signature and silently assume 'never sealed.' This is PLACE-ORIENTED in the worst way: a fact about the world is hardcoded. Either don't add the method until SealManager exists, or make it return an explicit `ErrNotImplemented` so callers can't accidentally rely on the false value.

issues.description: Sealed-error detection by string-Contains on error message is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE
issues.detail: `errwrap.Contains(err, consts.ErrNamespaceSealed.Error())` matches by substring of the error text. That complects identity (which sentinel) with value (message bytes). `errors.Is(err, consts.ErrNamespaceSealed)` is the simple version — sentinel identity, no string parsing, survives message edits. The existing ErrSealed check has the same flaw; this PR is the moment to stop propagating it.

issues.description: NSTokenLength = TokenLen + "."[1] + nsID conflates encoding with arithmetic
issues.detail: Per the description, token length is computed as `TokenLen + "."[1] + nsID`. Indexing a string literal to get a byte and adding it as a number is INCIDENTAL-COMPLEXITY — the '.' is a separator, not a quantity. The simple form is `TokenLen + 1 + len(nsID)` with a named constant `nsSeparatorLen = 1`. The current expression reads like a typo and will get 'fixed' wrong by someone later.

issues.description: ListAllNamespaces semantics changed implicitly via stubbed sealed-filtering — time semantics unclear
issues.detail: Callers (`loadLoginMFAConfigs`, `runLockedUserEntryUpdates`, `entityGaugeCollector`, `countActiveTokens`) all switched from `namespaceStore.ListAllNamespaces(ctx, true)` to `c.ListNamespaces(ctx)`. The set of namespaces returned at time T now depends on a not-yet-implemented seal predicate. What does 'all namespaces' mean — at what moment, including or excluding sealed ones? Document the time semantics before the stub becomes real, or every caller will mean something different.

issues.description: Test ctx threading shows the missing abstraction: requests should carry namespace as a value, not as ambient context
issues.detail: The diff sprinkles `namespace.RootContext(t.Context())` across a dozen test sites and replaces `context.Background()` mid-function. This is PLACE-ORIENTED test setup — the namespace is a load-bearing value being smuggled through context.Value. A `Request` value with an explicit `Namespace` field would make tests trivial and remove the entire class of 'forgot to wrap context' bugs. Not blocking this PR, but worth a hammock session before the next one.

review.summary: This PR is mostly threading namespace through context and reshaping ACL.root from a bool into a namespace pointer. The reshape is COMPLECTED: one field now carries 'is root policy', 'which namespace scope', and an implicit ancestry check evaluated lazily at request time. The `NamespaceSealed` stub that always returns false is a fact-shaped lie that downstream callers will quietly depend on. Error matching via substring-Contains and the `TokenLen + \".\"[1] + nsID` length expression are incidental complexity that should be replaced with `errors.Is` and explicit separator arithmetic. The deeper question that should have been asked first: should namespace be an ambient context value at all, or a load-bearing field on Request and ACL — the test churn in this diff is the field telling you.
